5547.d: Anointed One; the Messiah, the Christ. From chrio; Anointed One, i.e. The Messiah, an epithet of Jesus.

5207.d: A son, descendent. Apparently a primary word; a |son|, used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship.

5329.d: Perez, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus. Of Hebrew origin; Phares, an Israelite.

5601.d: Obed. Of Hebrew origin; Obed, an Israelite.

5316.d: Prolongation for the base of phos; to lighten, i.e. Show.

5399.d: To frighten, i.e. to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. Revere.

5088.d: A strengthened form of a primary teko tek'-o; to produce, literally or figuratively.

5259.d: Under, i.e. of place, or with verbs; of place (underneath) or where (below) or time (when).

5258.d: Sleep; fig: spiritual sleep. From an obsolete primary; sleep, i.e. spiritual torpor.

5613.d: Which how, i.e. In that manner.

5015.d: To disturb, agitate, stir up, trouble. Of uncertain affinity; to stir or agitate.

5119.d: Then, at that time. From ho and hote; the when, i.e. At the time that.

5550.d: A space of time or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay.

5463.d: To be |cheer|ful, i.e. Calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation, be well.

5479.d: Joy, gladness, a source of joy. From chairo; cheerfulness, i.e. Calm delight.

5557.d: Gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin.

5537.d: To utter an oracle, i.e. Divinely intimate; by implication, to constitute a firm for business, i.e. bear as a title.

5561.d: Feminine of a derivative of the base of chasma through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. A space of territory.

5343.d: To flee, escape, shun. Apparently a primary verb; to run away; by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish.

5054.d: End of life, death. From teleutao; decease.

5456.d: A tone; by implication, an address, saying or language.

5043.d: A child, descendent, inhabitant. From the base of timoria; a child.

5053.d: To end, finish, die, complete. From a presumed derivative of teleo; to finish life, i.e. Expire.

5590.d: Breath, i.e. spirit, abstractly or concretely.

5147.d: A worn path, beaten way, road, highway. From tribo; a rut or worn track.

5160.d: Food, nourishment, maintenance. From trepho; nourishment; by implication, rations.

5330.d: A separatist, i.e. Exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary.

5101.d: Who, which, what, why. Probably emphatic of tis; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what.

5263.d: To indicate, intimate, suggest, show, prove. From hupo and deiknuo; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. to exemplify.

5204.d: Water. And genitive case, hudatos, etc. From the base of huetos; water literally or figuratively.

5266.d: A sandal; anything bound under. From hupodeo; something bound under the feet, i.e. A shoe or sandal.

5532.d: Employment, i.e. An affair; also occasion, demand, requirement or destitution.

5616.d: As if, as it were, like; with numbers: about. From hos and ei; as if.

5062.d: Forty. The decade of tessares; forty.

5305.d: Lastly, afterward, later. Neuter of husteros as adverb; more lately, i.e. Eventually.

5346.d: To say, declare. Properly, the same as the base of phos and phaino; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. Speak or say.

5217.d: To go away, depart, begone, die. From hupo and ago; to lead under, i.e. Withdraw or retire, literally or figuratively.

5457.d: Light, a source of light, radiance. From an obsolete phao; luminousness.

5526.d: To feed, satisfy, fatten. From chortos; to fodder, i.e. to gorge.

5574.d: To deceive, lie, speak falsely. Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood.

5087.d: To put, place, lay, set, fix, establish. A prolonged form of a primary theo to place.

5407.d: To murder, kill. From phoneus; to be a murderer.

5100.d: Any one, some one, a certain one or thing. An enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object.

5035.d: Quickly, speedily. Neuter singular of tachus; shortly, i.e. Without delay, soon, or suddenly, or readily.

5438.d: A guarding or, the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or, the time, literally or figuratively.

5286.d: A footstool. Neuter of a compound of hupo and pous; something under the feet, i.e. A foot-rest.

5509.d: A tunic, garment, undergarment. Of foreign origin; a tunic or shirt.

5228.d: Gen: in behalf of; acc: above.

5057.d: A publican, collector of taxes. From telos and oneomai; a tax-farmer, i.e. Collector of public revenue.

5618.d: Just as, as, even as. From hos and per; just as, i.e. Exactly like.

5273.d: An actor under an assumed character, i.e. a dissembler

5368.d: To be a friend to (an individual or an object), i.e. Have affection for; specially, to kiss.

5009.d: A store-chamber, secret chamber, closet; a granary, barn.

5460.d: Bright, luminous, full of light. From phos; lustrous, i.e. Transparent or well-illuminated.

5142.d: Properly, to stiffen, i.e. Fatten (with food, etc.), pamper, rear).

5528.d: Grass, herbage, growing grain, hay. Apparently a primary word; a |court| or |garden|, i.e. herbage or vegetation.

5535.d: To need, have need of, want, desire. From chreia; to make necessity, i.e. Be in want of.

5519.d: A swine, hog, sow. Of uncertain derivation; a hog.

5578.d: A spurious prophet, i.e. Pretended foreteller or religious impostor.

5146.d: A thistle. From treis and belos; properly, a crow-foot, i.e. a thorny plant.

5429.d: Intelligent, prudent, sensible, wise. From phren; thoughtful, i.e. Sagacious or discreet; in a bad sense conceited.

5055.d: (a) I end, finish, (b) I fulfill, accomplish, (c) I pay. From telos; to end, i.e. Complete, execute, conclude, discharge.

5118.d: So great, so large, so long, so many. From tosos and houtos; so vast as this, i.e. Such.

5454.d: A burrow, hole, den, lair. Of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place.

5620.d: So that, therefore, so then, so as to. From hos and te; so too, i.e. Thus therefore.

5219.d: To hear under, i.e. To listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority.

5221.d: To meet, go to meet. From hupo and a derivative of anti; to go opposite under, i.e. To encounter, fall in with.

5602.d: In this same spot, i.e. Here or hither.

5222.d: A meeting. From hupantao; an encounter or concurrence.

5108.d: (including the other inflections); from toi and houtos; truly this, i.e. Of this sort (to denote character or individuality).

5058.d: A tax-collector's office, toll-house. Neuter of a presumed derivative of telones; a tax-gatherer's place of business.

5501.d: Worse, more severe. Irregular comparative of kakos; from an obsolete equivalent cheres; more evil or aggravated.

5345.d: A report, fame, saying. From phemi; a saying, i.e. Rumor.

5185.d: Blind, physically or mentally. From, tuphoo; opaque, i.e. blind.

5376.d: Fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites.

5278.d: To stay under, i.e. Remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. Bear, have fortitude, persevere.

5056.d: (a) an end, (b) event or issue, (c) the principal end, aim, purpose, (d) a tax.

5593.d: Cool, cold; fig: cold-hearted. From psuchos; chilly.

5560.d: Lame, deprived of a foot, limping. Apparently a primary word; |halt|, i.e. Limping.

5409.d: To carry, wear, bear constantly. From phoros; to have a burden, i.e. to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment.

5314.d: A glutton. From phago; a glutton.

5384.d: Friendly; subst: a friend, an associate. Properly, dear, i.e. A friend; actively, fond, i.e. Friendly.

5523.d: Chorazin, a town of Galilee. Of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine.

5184.d: Tyre, an ancient city, the capital of Phoenicia. Of Hebrew origin: Tyrus, a place in Palestine.

5312.d: (a) I raise on high, lift up, (b) I exalt, set on high. From hupsos; to elevate.

5412.d: To load, burden; pass: To be laden. From phortos; to load up, i.e. to overburden with ceremony.

5011.d: Humble, lowly, in position or spirit (in a good sense). Of uncertain derivation; depressed, i.e. humiliated.

5543.d: Useful, gentle, pleasant, kind. From chraomai; employed, i.e. useful.

5413.d: A burden; the freight of a ship. Diminutive of phortos; an invoice, i.e. a task or service.

5089.d: To pluck, pluck off. Perhaps akin to the alternate of haireomai, and thus to suro; to pull off.

5199.d: (a) sound, healthy, pure, whole, (b) wholesome. From the base of auzano; healthy, i.e. Well; figuratively, true.

5318.d: Apparent, clear, visible, manifest; adv: clearly. From phaino; shining, i.e. Apparent; neuter publicly, externally.

5188.d: To raise smoke, smolder. Apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. Slowly consume without flame.

5348.d: To be beforehand, i.e. Anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at.

5140.d: Three. Or neuter tria a primary number; |three|.

5117.d: A spot, i.e. Location; figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard.

5144.d: Thirty. The decade of treis; thirty.

5565.d: Apart from, separately from; without. Adverb from chora; at a space, i.e. Separately or apart from.

5045.d: A carpenter, an artisan. From the base of timoria; an artificer, i.e., a craftsman in wood.

5076.d: A tetrarch, ruler over a fourth part of a region. From tessares and archo; the ruler of a fourth part of a country.

5342.d: To carry, bear, bring; I conduct, lead; perhaps: I make publicly known. A primary verb.

5326.d: An apparition, ghost, spirit, phantom. From phantazo; a show, i.e. Spectre.

5401.d: (a) fear, terror, alarm, (b) the object or cause of fear, (c) reverence, respect. From a primary phebomai; alarm or fright.

5091.d: To prize, i.e. Fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere.

5623.d: To help, benefit, do good, be useful (to), profit. From the same as opheleia; to be useful, i.e. To benefit.

5451.d: A plant, that which is planted. From phuteuo; trans-planting, i.e. a shrub or vegetable.

5452.d: To plant, set. From a derivative of phuo; to set out in the earth, i.e. Implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine.

5419.d: To declare, explain, interpret. Probably akin to phrasso through the idea of defining; to indicate, i.e., to expound.

5562.d: To be in space, i.e. to pass, enter, or to hold, admit.

5408.d: Murder, slaughter, killing. From an obsolete primary pheno; murder.

5577.d: False testimony, false witness. From pseudomartur; untrue testimony.

5478.d: Canaanite, a Biblical and archaic name for Phoenician. From Chanaan; a Chanaanoean, or native of gentile Palestine.

5589.d: A crumb. Diminutive from a derivative of the base of psallo; a little bit or morsel.

5132.d: A table or stool, usually for food; also a counter for money.

5599.d: As a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh.

5070.d: Four thousand. From the multiplicative adverb of tessares and chilioi; four times a thousand.

5494.d: By implication, the rainy season, i.e. Winter.

5154.d: Third. Ordinal from treis; third; neuter a third part, or a third time, thirdly.

5426.d: (a) I think, (b) I think, judge, (c) I direct the mind to, seek for, (d) I observe, (e) I care for.

5013.d: To make or bring low, humble, humiliate; pass: To be humbled. From tapeinos; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate.

5137.d: The neck. Probably from trecho; the throat, i.e. life.

5007.d: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of tlao; a balance, i.e. a certain weight or |talent|.

5563.d: To place room between, i.e. Part; reflexively, to go away.

5083.d: To guard, i.e. To note; by implication, to detain; by extension, to withhold; by extension, to withhold.

5576.d: To testify falsely, bear false witness. From pseudomartur; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. Offer falsehood in evidence.

5442.d: To watch, i.e. Be on guard; by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid.

5302.d: To be later, i.e. to be inferior; generally, to fall short.

5225.d: To begin, am, exist, be in possession. From hupo and archomai; to begin under, i.e. Come into existence; expletively, to exist (verb).

5169.d: A hole; the eye of a needle. From a derivative of the base of trumalia; an aperture, i.e. A needle's eye.

5443.d: A tribe or race of people. From phuo; an offshoot, i.e. Race or clan.

5615.d: In like manner, likewise, just so. From hos and an adverb from autos; as thus, i.e. In the same way.

5455.d: To emit a sound; by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation.

5268.d: A beast of burden, an ass or mule. Neuter of a compound of hupo and zugos; an animal under the yoke, i.e., a donkey.

5614.d: Oh save!; hosanna, an exclamation of adoration.

5310.d: Highest, most high, the heights. Superlative from the base of hupsos; highest, i.e. the Supreme, or the heavens.

5444.d: A leaf. From the same as phule; a sprout, i.e. Leaf.

5418.d: A hedge, fence, partition. From phrasso; a fence, or inclosing barrier.

5022.d: A bull, an ox. Apparently a primary word; a bullock.

5195.d: To insult, treat with insolence. From hubris; to exercise violence, i.e. Abuse.

5037.d: And, both. A primary particle of connection or addition; both or also.

5392.d: To muzzle, silence. From phimos; to muzzle.

5270.d: Underneath, below, under. From hupo and kato; down under, i.e. Beneath.

5111.d: To dare, endure, be bold, have courage, make up the mind. From tolma; to venture; by implication, to be courageous.

5606.d: The shoulder. Perhaps from the alternate of phero; the shoulder.

5440.d: Neuter of a derivative of phulasso; a guard-case, i.e. |phylactery| for wearing slips of Scripture texts.

5028.d: A burial-place, sepulcher, tomb, grave. Masculine from thapto; a grave.

5611.d: Fair, beautiful, blooming. From hora; belonging to the right hour or season, i.e. flourishing (figuratively).

5272.d: Acting under a feigned part, i.e. deceit.

5158.d: A turn, i.e. mode or style; figuratively, deportment or character.

5604.d: The pain of childbirth, acute pain, severe agony, a snare. Akin to odune; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth.

5594.d: To cool, pass: I grow cold. A primary verb; to breathe, i.e. to chill.

5437.d: Flight, fleeing. From pheugo; a fleeing, i.e. Escape.

5580.d: A false Christ, pretended Messiah. From pseudes and Christos; a spurious Messiah.

5059.d: A wonder, portent, marvel. Of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen.

5338.d: Brightness, light, splendor, radiance. Probably akin to the base of phos; brilliancy.

5064.d: Four. Or neuter tessara a plural number; four.

5176.d: To eat, partake of a meal.

5549.d: To delay, tarry, linger, spend time. From chronos; to take time, i.e. Linger.

5180.d: To beat, strike, wound, inflict punishment.

5133.d: A money-changer, banker. From trapeza; a money-broker or banker.

5110.d: Interest, usury. From the base of tikto; interest on money loaned.

5165.d: A deep dish, platter, bowl. Neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl.

5214.d: To sing, sing hymns to, praise. From humnos; to hymn, i.e. Sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate in song.

5151.d: Three times. Adverb from treis; three times.

5564.d: A place, piece of land, field, property, estate. Diminutive of chora; a spot or plot of ground.

5621.d: An ear. Diminutive of ous; an earlet, i.e. One of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear.

5575.d: A false witness. From pseudes and a kindred form of martus; a spurious witness, i.e. Bearer of untrue testimony.

5092.d: A price, honor. From tino; a value, i.e. Money paid, or valuables; by analogy, esteem, or the dignity itself.

5027.d: A burial, burial place. Feminine from thapto; burial.

5355.d: Envy, a grudge, spite. Probably akin to the base of phtheiro; ill-will, i.e. Jealousy.

5417.d: To flagellate, scourge. From a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. Lash as a public punishment.

5511.d: A short cloak, worn by military officers and soldiers. Of uncertain derivation; a military cloak.

5521.d: Gall, bitter herbs. Feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as Chloe; |gall| or bile, i.e. poison or an anodyne.

5143.d: Which uses dremo drem'-o as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily.

5122.d: By name. Contraction for the neuter of ho and onoma; the name.

5510.d: Snow. Perhaps akin to the base of chasma or cheimon; snow.

5021.d: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. Assign or dispose.

5320.d: Clearly, openly, manifestly. Adverb from phaneros; plainly, i.e. Clearly or publicly.

5465.d: To let down, lower, slacken, loosen. From the base of chasma; to lower.

5319.d: To make clear (visible, manifest), make known. From phaneros; to render apparent.

5141.d: To tremble, be afraid. Strengthened from a primary treo; to |tremble| or fear.

5008.d: (Aramaic), girl, little girl. Of Chaldee origin; the fresh, i.e. Young girl; talitha.

5265.d: To bind under one's feet, i.e. Put on shoes or sandals.

5522.d: Earth, soil, dust. From the base of cheimon; a heap, i.e. Rubbish; loose dirt.

5506.d: A commander of a thousand men, a military tribune. From chilioi and archo; the commander of a thousand soldiers

5515.d: Green, pale green. From the same as Chloe; greenish, i.e. Verdant, dun-colored.

5473.d: A bronze vessel, brazen utensil. Diminutive from chalkos; a copper dish.

5243.d: Pride, arrogance, disdain. From huperephanos; haughtiness.

5249.d: Superabundantly, beyond measure. From huper and perissos; superabundantly, i.e. Exceedingly.

5081.d: Clearly, distinctly, plainly. Adverb from a compound of a derivative of telos and auge; in a far-shining manner, i.e. Plainly.

5149.d: To grate, gnash (as the teeth). Apparently a primary verb; to creak, i.e. to grate the teeth.

5536.d: Money, riches, possessions. Something useful or needed, i.e. Wealth, price.

5168.d: The eye of a needle. From a derivative of truo; an orifice, i.e. Needle's eye.

5090.d: Timaeus, father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus. Probably of Chaldee origin; Timoeus, an Israelite.

5276.d: Neuter of a presumed compound of hupo and lenos; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. Lower wine-vat.

5503.d: Feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of chasma through the idea of deficiency; a widow, literally or figuratively.

5304.d: Poverty, want, need. A falling short, i.e., penury.

5145.d: Three hundred. Plural from treis and hekaton; three hundred.

5499.d: Done or made with hands, artificial. From cheir and a derivative of poieo; manufactured, i.e. Of human construction.

5156.d: A trembling, quaking, fear. From tremo; a |trembling|, i.e. Quaking with fear.

5023.d: This; he, she, it. Nominative or accusative case neuter plural of houtos; these things.

5010.d: Regular arrangement, i.e. fixed succession, official dignity.

5428.d: Mental action or activity, i.e. Intellectual or moral insight.

5487.d: To favor, bestow freely on. From charis; to grace, i.e. Indue with special honor.

5050.d: Completion, fulfillment, perfection. From phusioo; completion, i.e. verification, or absolution.

5014.d: Abasement (in spirit), low condition (in circumstances). From tapeinoo; depression.

5244.d: Proud, arrogant, disdainful. From huper and phaino; appearing above others, i.e. haughty.

5290.d: To turn back, return. From hupo and strepho; to turn under, i.e. To return.

5311.d: Height, heaven; dignity, eminence. From a derivative of huper; elevation, i.e. altitude, the sky, or dignity.

5336.d: A manger, feeding-trough, stall. From pateomai; a crib.

5167.d: A turtle-dove. From truzo; a turtle-dove.

5323.d: Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess. Of Hebrew origin; Phanuel, an Israelite.

5048.d: To complete, i.e. accomplish, or consummate.

5086.d: Probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor.

5075.d: To rule over as a tetrarch. From tetrarches; to be a tetrarch.

5139.d: Rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria.

5327.d: A valley, ravine, chasm, cleft. Properly, strengthened from the base of peran or rather of rhegnumi; a gap or chasm, i.e. Ravine.

5138.d: Rough, rugged, uneven. Perhaps strengthened from the base of rhegnumi; uneven, rocky.

5317.d: Peleg, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus. Of Hebrew origin; Phalek, a patriarch.

5548.d: To smear or rub with oil, i.e. to consecrate to an office or religious service.

5298.d: To withdraw, retire, go back, retreat. From hupo and choreo; to vacate down, i.e. Retire quietly.

5198.d: To have sound health, i.e. Be well; figuratively, to be uncorrupt.

5597.d: To rub, rub to pieces. Prolongation from the same base as psallo; to triturate, i.e. to rub out.

5212.d: Your, yours. From humeis; yours, i.e. Pertaining to you.

5240.d: To pour out so that it overflows. From huper and the alternate form of ekcheo; to pour out over, i.e. to overflow.

5166.d: To gather (as of grapes), harvest. From a derivative of trugo meaning ripe fruit; to collect the vintage.

5483.d: (a) To show favor to, (b) To pardon, forgive, (c) To show kindness.

5533.d: A debtor. From a derivative of chrao and opheiletes; a loan-ower, i.e. Indebted person.

5274.d: (a) I take up, (b) I welcome, entertain, (c) I answer, (d) I suppose, imagine.

5370.d: A kiss. From phileo; a kiss.

5484.d: Accusative case of charis as preposition; through favor of, i.e. On account of.

5529.d: Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas. Of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod.

5453.d: To grow, grow up, spring up.

5052.d: To bring to maturity. From a compound of telos and phero; to be a bearer to completion, i.e. To ripen fruit.

5281.d: Endurance, steadfastness, patient waiting for. From hupomeno; cheerful endurance, constancy.

5134.d: A wound. From the base of titrosko; a wound.

5264.d: To admit under one's roof, i.e. Entertain hospitably.

5531.d: To lend. Probably the same as the base of chraomai; to loan.

5609.d: An egg. Apparently a primary word; an |egg|.

5461.d: To shed rays, i.e. To shine or to brighten up.

5203.d: Afflicted with dropsy. From a compound of hudor and a derivative of optanomai; to be |dropsical|.

5421.d: A pit, well, cistern. Of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground, i.e. A cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss.

5030.d: Soon, quickly, hastily. Adverb from tachus; briefly, i.e. speedily, or rapidly.

5585.d: To reckon, compute, calculate. From psephos; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. to compute.

5505.d: A thousand, the number one thousand. From chilioi; one thousand.

5525.d: A dance, dancing. Of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. Round dance

5430.d: Wisely, sensibly, prudently. Adverb from phronimos; prudently.

5366.d: Money-loving, avaricious, covetous. From philos and arguros; fond of silver, i.e. Avaricious.

5395.d: A flame. From a primary phlego; a blaze.

5490.d: A gap, gulf, chasm. From a form of an obsolete primary chao; a |chasm| or vacancy.

5299.d: To hit under the eye, i.e. to tease or annoy, subdue.

5034.d: Quickness, speed; hastily, immediately. From the same as tachus; a brief space, i.e. in haste.

5073.d: Four-fold, four times as much. From tessares and a derivative of the base of pleistos; quadruple.

5291.d: To spread under, strew under. From hupo and stronnumi; to strew underneath.

5482.d: A palisade, mound for besieging. From charasso; a stake, i.e. a palisade or rampart.

5135.d: To wound. From trauma; to inflict a wound.

5271.d: To act the part, pretend; I answer, respond. Middle voice from hupo and krino; to decide under a false part, i.e. dissemble.

5411.d: A tax, tribute, especially on persons. From phero; a load, i.e. a tax.

5106.d: Indeed now, therefore, accordingly, well then. From toi and nun; truly now, i.e. Accordingly.

5177.d: (a) gen: I obtain, (b) absol: I chance, happen; ordinary, everyday, it may chance, perhaps.

5568.d: A set piece of music, i.e. A sacred ode; collectively, the book of the Psalms.

5400.d: Neuter of a derivative of phobeo; a frightening thing, i.e. Terrific portent.

5584.d: To manipulate, i.e. Verify by contact; figuratively, to search for.

5504.d: Yesterday. Of uncertain derivation; |yesterday|; by extension, in time past or hitherto.

5085.d: Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine.

5520.d: To be angry with. From chole; to be bilious, i.e. irritable.

5579.d: A lie, falsehood, untruth; false religion. From pseudomai; a falsehood.

5476.d: Adverb perhaps from the base of chasma through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. Prostrate.

5404.d: A palm tree, the date-palm. Of uncertain derivation; a palm-tree.

5186.d: To make blind, physically or mentally. From tuphlos; to make blind, i.e. to obscure.

5040.d: A little child. Diminutive of teknon; an infant, i.e. darlings.

5493.d: A storm-brook, a winter torrent. From the base of cheimon and rheo; a storm-runlet, i.e. Winter-torrent.

5322.d: A torch, lantern, light. From phaino; a lightener, i.e. Light; lantern.

5102.d: A title, inscription. Of Latin origin; a titulus or |title|.

5307.d: Woven. From huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. knitted.

5301.d: Hyssop, a stalk or stem of hyssop. Of foreign origin; |hyssop|.

5179.d: A die, i.e. a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. A statue, style or resemblance; specially, a sampler, i.e. A model or instance.

5039.d: A sign, certain proof. Neuter of a presumed derivative of tekmar; a token, i.e. Criterion of certainty.

5253.d: Neuter of a derivative of huper; a higher part of the house, i.e. Apartment in the third story.

5435.d: Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor.

5512.d: To mock, scoff, jest, jeer. From a derivative probably of cheilos; to throw out the lip, i.e. Jeer at.

5153.d: Three thousand. From tris and chilioi; three times a thousand.

5553.d: A piece of gold, golden ornament. Diminutive of chrusos; a golden article, i.e. Gold plating, ornament, or coin.

5433.d: To be wanton, insolent; I roar, rage. Akin to bruo, brucho; to snort, i.e. to make a tumult.

5441.d: A guard, keeper, sentinel. From phulasso; a watcher or sentry.

5071.d: Four hundred. Plural from tessares and hekaton; four hundred.

5096.d: Timon, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem. From time; valuable; Timon, a Christian.

5260.d: To throw in stealthily, i.e. Introduce by collusion.

5571.d: False, deceitful, lying, untrue. From pseudomai; untrue, i.e. Erroneous, deceitful, wicked.

5488.d: Haran. Of Hebrew origin; Charrhan, a place in Mesopotamia.

5466.d: A Chaldean. Probably of Hebrew or; a Chaldoean, or native or the region of the lower Euphrates.

5328.d: Pharaoh, the title of ancient Egyptian kings. Of foreign origin; Pharao, an Egyptian king.

5477.d: Chanaan, the early name of Palestine.

5527.d: Food, sustenance, provision. From chortazo; forage, i.e. Food.

5608.d: To buy, purchase. Middle voice from an apparently primary onos; to purchase.

5063.d: Forty years of age. From tessarakonta and etos; of forty years of age.

5255.d: Listening to, obedient, submissive. From hupakouo; attentively listening, i.e. submissive.

5496.d: To lead by the hand. From cheiragogos; to be a hand-leader, i.e. To guide.

5018.d: Belonging to Tarsus, a Tarsian. From Tarsos; a Tarsean, i.e. Native of Tarsus.

5038.d: A wall, especially of a city. Akin to the base of tikto; a wall.

5019.d: Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia. Perhaps the same as tarsos; Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor.

5000.d: Antelope; Tabitha, a Christian woman at Joppa. Of Chaldee origin; the gazelle; Tabitha, a Christian female.

5074.d: Four-footed. From tessares and pous; a quadruped.

5403.d: Phoenicia, a northern coast strip of the Roman province Syria. From phoinix; palm-country; Phoenice, a region of Palestine.

5546.d: A Christian. From Christos; a Christian, i.e. Follower of Christ.

5069.d: Neuter of a presumed derivative of tetras; a quaternion or squad of four Roman soldiers.

5017.d: A disturbance, commotion, trouble. Masculine from tarasso; a disturbance, i.e. tumult.

5183.d: A Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre. From Turos; a Tyrian, i.e. Inhabitant of Tyrus.

5002.d: Appointed, arranged, fixed. From tasso; arranged, i.e. Appointed or stated.

r: someone to lead him by the hand

5159.d: To endure the ways of, put up with. From tropos and phoreo; to endure one's habits.

5282.d: To conjecture, suppose, suspect, deem. From hupo and noieo; to think under, i.e. To surmise or conjecture.

5256.d: To minister to, serve. From huperetes; to be a subordinate, i.e. subserve.

5205.d: Rain. From a primary huo; rain, especially a shower.

5500.d: To be a hand-reacher or voter, i.e. to select or appoint.

5095.d: Timothy, a Christian of Lystra, helper of Paul. From time and theos; dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian.

5174.d: Troas, a harbor city of Mysia. From Tros; the Troad, i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor.

5375.d: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia. Plural of Philippos; Philippi, a place in Macedonia.

5033.d: Neuter plural of the superlative of tachus; most quickly, i.e. as soon as possible.

5386.d: A philosopher. From philos and sophos; fond of wise things, i.e. A |philosopher|.

5480.d: Sculpture; engraving, a stamp, sign. From the same as charax; a scratch or etching, i.e. Stamp, or scupltured figure.

5078.d: Art, skill, trade, craft. From the base of tikto; art, i.e., a trade, or skill.

5237.d: To overlook, take no notice of, disregard. From huper and eido; to overlook, i.e. Not punish.

5181.d: A provincial form of the derivative of the base of kurios; a |tyrant|; Tyrannus, an Ephesian.

5559.d: The skin, surface of the body. Probably akin to the base of chraomai through the idea of handling; the body.

5079.d: A craftsman, artisan, architect, builder. From techne; an artisan; figuratively, a founder.

5190.d: Fortuitous, i.e. Fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian.

5161.d: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia. From trophe; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian.

5508.d: Chios, an island in the Mediterranean.

5551.d: To be a time-wearer, i.e. To procrastinate.

5012.d: Humility, lowliness of mind, modesty. From a compound of tapeinos and the base of phren; humiliation of mind, i.e. Modesty.

5288.d: To withhold under, i.e. to cower or shrink, to conceal.

5339.d: To spare, abstain, forbear. Of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. to abstain or to treat leniently.

5148.d: A space of three years. From a compound of treis and etos; a three years' period.

5334.d: Report, tidings, information. From phemi; a saying, i.e. Report.

5097.d: To punish, avenge myself on. From a comparative of time and ouros; properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. To avenge.

5439.d: To imprison, deliver into custody. From phulax; to incarcerate.

5109.d: A wall. Another form of teichos; a wall.

5061.d: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of Paul at Caesarea. Of uncertain derivation; Tertullus, a Roman.

5335.d: To assert, affirm, profess. Prolongation from the same as phemi; to assert.

5347.d: Festus. Of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus, a Roman.

5325.d: Show, display, pomp, imagination. From a derivative of phantazo; a show.

5586.d: A pebble, i.e. a verdict or ticket; a vote.

5530.d: To use, make use of, deal with, take advantage of.

5364.d: Humanely, kindly. Adverb from a compound of philos and anthropos; fondly to man, i.e. Humanely.

5284.d: To sail under. From hupo and pleo; to sail under the lee of.

5196.d: (a) insult, injury, outrage, (b) damage, loss. From huper; insolence, i.e. Insult, injury.

5405.d: Phoenix, a bay on the south coast of Crete. Probably the same as phoinix; Phoenix, a place in Crete.

5566.d: The north-west wind, and the quarter of the sky from which it comes. Of Latin origin; the north-west wind.

5285.d: To blow gently. From hupo and pneo; to breathe gently, i.e. Breeze.

5189.d: Violent, tempestuous, stormy. From a derivative of tupho; stormy.

5295.d: To run under shelter of. From hupo and trecho; to run under, i.e., to sail past.

5269.d: To under-gird, as to strengthen a ship against the waves. From hupo and zonnumi; to gird under, i.e. Frap.

5492.d: To be storm-tossed. From the same as cheimon; to storm, i.e. to labor under a gale.

5065.d: Fourteenth. From tessares and kai and dekatos; fourteenth.

5363.d: Love of mankind, benevolence. From the same as philanthropos; fondness of mankind, i.e. Benevolence.

5434.d: A dry stick for burning. Neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo; something desiccated, i.e. A dry twig.

5390.d: Kindly, in a friendly manner. Adverb from philophron; with friendliness of mind, i.e. Kindly.

5410.d: A forum or market-place; only in comparative with Appios; a station on the Appian road.

5218.d: Obedience, submissiveness, compliance. From hupakouo; attentive hearkening, i.e. compliance or submission.

5486.d: A gratuity, i.e. Deliverance;, a endowment, i.e. religious qualification, or miraculous faculty.

5349.d: Corruptible, perishable. From phtheiro; decayed, i.e. perishable.

5446.d: Natural, (a) according to nature, (b) merely animal. From phusis; |physical|, i.e. instinctive.

5540.d: Use, manner of use. From chraomai; employment, i.e., sexual intercourse.

5449.d: Growth, i.e. natural production; by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage.

5582.d: A falsehood, lie, untruthfulness. From pseudomai; a fabrication, i.e. Falsehood.

5004.d: Hardship, misery, distress, toil. From talaiporos; wretchedness, i.e. Calamity.

5267.d: Answerable to, liable to (brought under) the judgment of. From hupo and dike; under sentence, i.e. condemned.

5236.d: A throwing beyond others, i.e. supereminence; adverbially pre- eminently.

5005.d: Wretched, afflicted, miserable. From the base of talanton and a derivative of the base of peira; enduring trial, i.e. Miserable.

5427.d: Thought, purpose, aspirations. From phroneo; inclination or purpose.

5206.d: The placing as a son, i.e. Adoption.

5356.d: Corruption, destruction, decay, rottenness, decomposition. From phtheiro; decay, i.e. Ruin.

5241.d: To intercede for, make petition for. From huper and entugchano; to intercede in behalf of.

5245.d: To be more than conqueror, prevail mightily. From huper and nikao; to vanquish beyond, i.e. Gain a decisive victory.

5353.d: A sound. From phtheggomai; utterance, i.e. A musical note.

5538.d: An oracle, divine response. From chrematizo; a divine response or revelation.

5252.d: To have high notions, be over-proud. From huper and phroneo; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. Be vain or arrogant.

5387.d: Fond of natural relatives, i.e. Fraternal towards fellow Christian.

5360.d: Brotherly love, love of Christian brethren. From philadelphos; fraternal affection.

5381.d: Love to strangers, hospitality. From philoxenos; hospitableness.

5595.d: To feed, dole out. From the base of psomion; to supply with bits, i.e. to nourish.

5389.d: To be zealous, strive eagerly, desire very strongly.

5402.d: Phoebe, a Christian woman in the church at Cenchreae. Feminine of phoibos; Phoebe, a Christian woman.

5247.d: Superiority, excellence, preeminence, authority. From huperecho; prominence, i.e. superiority.

5051.d: A perfecter, completer, finisher. From teleioo; a completer, i.e. Consummater.

5163.d: The track of a wheel, a path. From trochos; a track, i.e. a course of conduct.

5324.d: To cause to appear, make visible. From a derivative of phaino; to make apparent, i.e. to appear.

5226.d: To yield, submit to authority. From hupo and eiko; to surrender.

5157.d: A turning, change, mutation. From an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn, i.e. Revolution.

5036.d: Quick, swift, speedy, ready, prompt. Of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. prompt or ready.

5468.d: To bridle, curb, restrain, sway. From a compound of chalinos and the reduplicated form of ago; to be a bit-leader, i.e. To curb.

5554.d: Adorned with a gold ring. From chrusos and daktulios; gold-ringed, i.e. Wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry.

5425.d: To shudder, shiver, tremble. Apparently a primary verb; to |bristle| or chill, i.e. Shudder.

5469.d: A bridle, bit. From chalao; a curb or head-stall.

5208.d: Wood, fuel. Perhaps akin to xulon; a forest, i.e. fuel.

5394.d: To inflame, fire with passion, set on fire, burn up. From phlox; to cause a blaze, i.e. Ignite.

5164.d: A wheel, course. From trecho; a wheel, i.e. a circuit of physical effects.

5534.d: It is necessary, proper, fitting. Third person singular of the same as chraomai or chrao used impersonally; it needs be.

5373.d: Friendship, affection, fondness, love. From philos; fondness.

5003.d: To endure severe hardship, be harassed, complain. From talaiporos; to be wretched, i.e. Realize one's own misery.

5171.d: To live a luxurious life, live self-indulgently. From truphe; to indulge in luxury.

5049.d: Perfectly, completely, without wavering. Adverb from teleios; completely, i.e. without wavering.

5277.d: To leave behind. A prolonged form for hupoleipo; to leave behind, i.e. Bequeath.

5261.d: A writing-copy, an example, pattern. From a compound of hupo and grapho; an underwriting, i.e. Copy for imitation.

5361.d: Loving like a brother, loving one's brethren. From philos and adephos; fond of brethren, i.e. Fraternal.

5612.d: To roar, howl, as a beast. Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to |roar|.

5031.d: Swift, quick, impending. From tachos; curt, i.e. Impending.

5107.d: From a derivative of toi and de; such-like then, i.e. So great.

5459.d: (lit: light-bearing), radiant, the morning-star. From phos and phero; light-bearing, i.e., the morning-star.

5572.d: A spurious teacher, i.e. Propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine.

5020.d: To thrust down to Tartarus or Gehenna. From Tartaros; to incarcerate in eternal torment.

5077.d: To reduce to ashes, consume, destroy. From tephra; to incinerate, i.e. Consume.

5113.d: A daring, bold man. From tolmao; a daring man.

5246.d: Immoderate, boastful, excessive, pompous. From huper and ogkos; bulging over, i.e. insolent.

5300.d: A hog, boar, or sow. Apparently a primary word; a hog.

5507.d: A thousand. Plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand.

5080.d: To make liquid; pass: I melt (away). Apparently a primary verb; to liquefy.

5545.d: An anointing. From chrio; an unguent or smearing, i.e. the special endowment of the Holy Spirit.

5489.d: Papyrus, paper. From the same as charax; a sheet of writing-material.

5383.d: To be fond of being first, i.e. Ambitious of distinction.

5396.d: To be a babbler or trifler, i.e. to berate idly or mischievously.

5254.d: To submit to, undergo, suffer. From hupo and echo; to hold oneself under, i.e. Endure with patience.

5447.d: By nature, naturally. Adverb from phusikos; |physically|, i.e. instinctively.

5352.d: Autumnal, in autumn, when fruit is expected. From derivative of phthino and opora; autumnal.

5598.d: Omega, the last letter of the Greek alphabet. The last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. the finality.

5359.d: Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia. From Philadelphos, a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor.

5474.d: Neuter of a compound of chalkos and libanos; burnished copper, an alloy of copper and silver having a brilliant lustre.

5513.d: Warm, tepid; of persons: lukewarm. From chlio; tepid.

5193.d: Glassy, made of glass, transparent. From hualos; glassy, i.e. Transparent.

5357.d: A shallow and flat bowl. Of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup.

5115.d: A bow. From the base of tikto; a bow.

5518.d: A Greek dry measure, equivalent to 1.92 pints. Of uncertain derivation; a choenix or certain dry measure.

5155.d: Made of hair. From thrix; hairy, i.e. Made of hair.

5191.d: Dark purple or blue, of the color of hyacinth. From huakinthos; |hyacinthine| or |jacinthine|, i.e. Deep blue.

5470.d: Made of bronze, bronze, brass. From chalkos; coppery.

5333.d: A magician, sorcerer. The same as pharmakeus.

5006.d: A talent in weight. From talanton; talent-like in weight.

5558.d: To gild, adorn with gold. From chrusos; to gild, i.e. Bespangle with golden ornaments.

5094.d: Preciousness, costliness, worth. From timios; expensiveness, i.e. magnificence.

5068.d: Square, four-cornered. From tessares and gonia; four-cornered, i.e. Square.

5194.d: Glass, crystal, clear transparent stone. Perhaps from the same as huetos; glass.

5472.d: Chalcedony, a small stone of various colors. From chalkos and perhaps eidos; copper-like, i.e. |chalcedony|.

5555.d: A topaz, a gem with a bright yellow color. From chrusos and lithos; gold-stone, i.e. A yellow gem.

5116.d: Topaz. Neuter of a presumed derivative of topazos; a gem, probably the chrysolite.

5556.d: A chrysoprase, gem of a golden-greenish color. From chrusos and prason; a greenish-yellow gem.

5192.d: The |hyacinth| or |jacinth|, i.e. Some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon.
